# Contract fixtures: what Pi Durable Platform really sends

Tokens and key sets in this directory were produced by Pi Durable Platform's own code,
not by a reimplementation, and are checked by `../../contract_pdp_test.go` against
this package's verifier (`Service.Verify`, `Service.Test`).

## How they were generated

* PDP: `pi-durable-platform` v0.4.0 (`HEAD` of the owner's checkout, exported read-only with
  `git archive` to a scratch directory; nothing was run in or changed in the checkout).
* Tokens: `internal/mcp.(*Service).identityToken` (the function the MCP gateway calls for every
  forwarded request) -> `internal/mcpidentity.(*Keys).Sign`, against a scratch Postgres seeded with a
  personal workspace, a shared team, users (active, suspended, not a member), private/shared/unknown
  threads and a running trigger run. `Keys.Now` was set to a fixed clock
  (`2026-10-20T12:00:00Z` = iat 1792497600 for the main set).
* Key sets: `internal/mcpidentity.(*Keys).ServeJWKS` (the handler behind
  `GET /.well-known/mcp-identity-jwks.json`) driven with `httptest`; body and the two headers it sets
  (`Content-Type: application/jwk-set+json`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`) are saved as
  `jwks/<name>.json` and `jwks/<name>.headers.json`. `jwks/real-http-response-headers.json` is the same
  handler over a real HTTP connection (Content-Length, Date added by net/http); through PDP's full router
  (`httpapi.NewAPIHandler`) the answer is identical plus `X-Request-Id`, `X-Content-Type-Options`,
  `Referrer-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options`.
* Rotation: `Keys.Rotate` (prepublish 1h, then `Now`+`DropPrevious`) at moved fixed clocks, so
  `jwks-prepublished`, `jwks-overlap`, `jwks-retired-old-key-gone`, `jwks-after-drop-previous` are PDP's
  published sets at those instants.
* Throwaway key: every signing key was generated by PDP (`Keys.Ensure`/`Rotate`) inside a scratch database
  and sealed with a throwaway `ENCRYPTION_KEY`; the database was discarded. Only public JWK members
  (`use, kty, kid, crv, alg, x, y`) are stored here and the tokens were signed once. There is no private
  key anywhere in these files, and the keys sign nothing real.
* The generator (a `_test.go` file for PDP's `internal/mcp/` that mints the tokens, and a small script that
  reshapes its output) is not part of this repository, because it needs a PDP source tree. Each run makes new
  keys and kids, so regenerating changes every file: the fixtures are meant to be frozen; regenerate them only
  when PDP's token format changes, from PDP's own tree.

## Files

* `tokens/<name>.jwt`: the compact token exactly as PDP produced it.
* `tokens/<name>.decoded.json`: header and payload, for humans (not used by the test).
* `tokens/<name>.expected.json`: what the portal must do. `checks[]`: `at` (the verifier's injected clock),
  `jwks` (which recorded key set the fake platform serves), `accept`/`reason` (a `Rejection.Reason`),
  optional `platformAudience`, `personIssuer`, `twice` (second use must be `replay`), and for accepted
  tokens the identity fields expected.

Platform the fixtures assume: issuer `https://agents.example.com`, audience (the portal's `APP_URL`, PDP's
`identityAudience`) `https://mcp.example.com`, portal `OIDC_ISSUER` (= `person.iss`)
`https://login.example.org/application/o/pdp/`.

| token | PDP scenario | expected |
|---|---|---|
| personal_private_email_portalaud | personal workspace, private thread, email on | accept; person+email, present; skew edges, replay, wrong audience, issuer slash |
| personal_private_noemail_serveraud | no `identityAudience`: aud = server URL | refuse `audience` (accept when the platform's audience is that URL) |
| team_private_member | team agent, private thread of a member | accept; person without email |
| team_shared_thread | team agent, shared thread | accept; no `person`, not present |
| personal_nothread_handshake | personal workspace, no thread | accept; owner named, `person_present` false, visibility `none`, no `tool` |
| personal_triggered_run | personal workspace, triggered run | accept; present false |
| rot_old_key_while_new_published | old key signs, new key already published | accept with both keys; `unknown_kid` once the key is withdrawn |
| rot_new_key | new key signs, old still published | accept with overlap set; `unknown_kid` with the stale set |

## Running

Needs the test Postgres like the other integration tests (`OMP_TEST_DATABASE_URL`):

    go test ./internal/agentidentity -run TestPDPContract -count=1
